title: Monitor Buying Signals on a List of Accounts
summary: Check a list of target accounts for the dated, public events that mean someone is in market: a job post for the role you sell into, a company saying something new, a detection feed firing. The commands with the Cargo CLI and the open-source monitor-buying-signals skill, free check first, what each check costs, and what a signal does not give you.
body_markdown:
**To monitor buying signals on a list of accounts, decide first which events would change what you say (hiring the role you sell into, a public statement about the problem, how fresh it must be), run the free detection check across the whole list, then pay for job-post and public-post lookups only on the accounts it did not cover.** Report one row per account that fired, with a date and a link, and nothing for the rest.


Fit tells you who to talk to; timing tells you when. The[monitor-buying-signals skill](https://www.getcargo.ai/skills/monitor-buying-signals) runs this from your coding agent, and every step below is a Cargo CLI call you can run yourself.


## Set it up#


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com
npx   skills   add   getcargohq/gtm-skills/monitor-buying-signals


```


A new account starts with 100 free credits and needs no card. Then ask your agent, for example: *“Watch our 20 open-opportunity accounts and tell me which started hiring RevOps in the last 30 days.”* The skill asks three questions before it runs anything: the role you sell into, what they would say in public if they had the problem, and how many days old a signal may be. A watchlist built without those answers returns everything and means nothing.


## The checks, cheapest first#


**1. The detection feed, free.** Sillage` searchLeads` reads the detections already delivered to a signal model in your workspace, filtered to your accounts. It costs 0, so it runs on the whole list.


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"sillage","actionSlug":"searchLeads"}'   \
--data   '{"modelUuid":"<your signal model>","companyDomains":["acme.com","globex.com"],"limit":100}'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


An empty result means nothing has been delivered for those accounts, not that no signal exists. Only the second justifies the paid checks.


**2. Job posts for the role you sell into.** TheirStack` searchJobs` , filtered by company domain, job title and age:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"theirStack","actionSlug":"searchJobs"}'   \
--data   '{
"companyFields": {"company_domain_or": ["acme.com","globex.com"]},
"fields": {"job_title_or": ["Head of RevOps","Revenue Operations"], "posted_at_max_age_days": 30},
"limit": 50
}'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


` posted_at_max_age_days` is the freshness number. Without it the search returns the back catalogue and every account looks like it is hiring.


**3. What the company said in public.** X` getUserPosts` on the company’s own handle, confirmed from its website first, because squatted and parody handles resolve fine:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"x","actionSlug":"getUserPosts"}'   \
--records   '[{"handle":"acme","limit":20}]'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


Cargo platform data, 90 days to Oct 16 2026: job-posting searches through TheirStack` searchJobs` ran 117,000 times on Cargo.


## What comes back#


One row per account that fired:


Column Why it is there


` signal` what happened, in words


` date` when; a signal with no date cannot be judged fresh


` source` the link; a trigger nobody can open is a rumour


` so_what` the one line on why it changes the conversation


Keep it separate from your fit score. A perfect-fit account with no trigger and a poor-fit account hiring aggressively can average to the same number, which hides both answers. How long each kind of signal stays worth acting on is its own decision: see[how long a buying signal is worth](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/buying-signal-time-decay) .


## What it costs#


Check Credits (list price)


Sillage` searchLeads` 0


TheirStack` searchJobs` 0.5 per job post returned


X` getUserPosts` 0.02 per package of up to 100 posts


Sample 10 to 20 accounts first and read two numbers: the cost, and how many accounts fired. If two in twenty fired, a weekly run over 500 accounts is worth it. If none did, the triggers are wrong and a wider run will not fix that. On a schedule, check only accounts whose last check is older than the interval, or every run re-bills accounts that did nothing.


## What it will not do#


- **Give you a reason to send.** A signal says a message might be relevant; it is not a lawful basis for sending one. “They are hiring” and “they posted about it” are not consent. Without a basis, the output is research.
- **Build lists from engagement.** Followers, likers and retweeters are out of scope: people who engaged with a post did not ask to hear from you.
- **Run on its own.** This skill is a one-off check from your agent. For a pipeline that keeps watching, the cookbooks deploy one:[new-hire-detection](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/new-hire-detection) for people who just took a role you sell to, and[social-listening](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/social-listening) for public conversations about your problem.


Run it with the[monitor-buying-signals skill](https://www.getcargo.ai/skills/monitor-buying-signals) .
